title: Permanent establishment — domestic s 6(1) and treaty Art 5
summary: Facet map: does a PE exist? Dual-track spine. DOMESTIC (s 6(1), no DTA): place at/through which business is carried on → inclusions (a) agent place, (b) substantial equipment, (c) construction project, (d) associated-entity goods with s 6(6) deeming → exclusions (e) bona fide commission agent, (f) no general authority agent, (g) purchasing-only place. TREATY (Art 5 via International Tax Agreements Act 1953 s 4(2)): fixed place of business (Art 5(1)) → inclusions (Art 5(2)) → preparatory/auxiliary exclusions (Art 5(3)) → dependent agent (Art 5(4)) → independent agent (Art 5(5)), subsidiary carve-out (Art 5(6)). FACETS: treaty priority and residual domestic role (International Tax Agreements Act 1953 s 4(2), s 23AH(15), s 44(7)), agency limbs comparison, attributable profits (TR 2001/11, Div 815), treaty variations (9 vs 12-month building sites). Subsection coverage: s 6(1) paras (a)-(g) + s 6(6) mapped; Art 5(1)-(7) mapped (US text as template). Rulings: TR 2002/5, LCG 2016/1, TR 2014/3, TR 2001/11.

nodes.label: A person (including a non-resident) carries on business activity in a jurisdiction — does a permanent establishment (PE) exist?
nodes.body: Single question with two definitional tracks: domestic (s 6(1) ITAA 1936) and treaty (Art 5 of the applicable DTA). The treaty track generally overrides for treaty residents (International Tax Agreements Act 1953 s 4(2)). Facets carry each limb.

nodes.label: Is the person a resident of a DTA country (relying on the treaty)?
nodes.body: If yes, Art 5 of the DTA applies (International Tax Agreements Act 1953 s 4(2) gives treaties priority over domestic law). If no DTA applies (non-treaty country, or non-treaty purposes), the domestic s 6(1) definition applies.

nodes.label: Apply the domestic s 6(1) PE definition
nodes.body: s 6(1) 'permanent establishment': a place at or through which the person carries on any business, with inclusions (paras (a)-(d)) and exclusions (paras (e)-(g)).

rulings.title: What is a place at or through which a person carries on any business

nodes.label: Is there a place at or through which the person carries on business?
nodes.body: The core test. TR 2002/5 and LCG 2016/1 explain what constitutes a place (premises, facilities, installations — owned or leased) and when business is carried on at or through it.

rulings.title: What is a place at or through which a person carries on any business
What is a place at or through which a person carries on any business

nodes.label: No fixed place — check inclusion/deeming limbs (s 6(1)(a)-(d))?
nodes.body: Without a fixed place, there is no PE under the core s 6(1) test. However, paras (a)-(d) may still deem a PE: (a) agent place, (b) substantial equipment/machinery, (c) construction project, (d) associated-entity goods. Also check s 6(6) deeming. The exclusions in paras (e)-(g) must then be considered.

nodes.label: Does an inclusion apply — agent place (a), substantial equipment (b), construction project (c), associated-entity goods (d)?
nodes.body: s 6(1) includes: (a) place where business is carried on through an agent; (b) place where the person has/is using/is installing substantial equipment or machinery; (c) construction project place; (d) where the person sells goods manufactured/assembled/processed/packed/distributed by another person for, or at or to the order of, the person — and either of those persons participates in the management, control or capital of the other person, or another person participates in the management, control or capital of both — the place where the goods are manufactured/assembled/processed/packed/distributed. s 6(6) deems the selling business to be carried on at the (d) place.

nodes.label: Does an exclusion apply — bona fide commission agent (e), no general authority agent (f), purchasing place (g)?
nodes.body: s 6(1) excludes: (e) bona fide commission agent/broker at customary rates (subject to 'unless the person otherwise carries on business there'); (f) agent without (or not habitually exercising) general authority to negotiate and conclude contracts, or whose stock-filling authority extends to filling orders from stock situated in the country where the place is located but is not regularly exercised (also subject to 'unless the person otherwise carries on business there'); (g) premises maintained solely for purchasing goods or merchandise (no 'otherwise carries on business' carve-out applies).

nodes.label: Confirm: Domestic PE exists
nodes.body: Consequences: business profits attributable to the Australian PE assessable; PE gates s 23AH, s 44(1)(c), Div 855, WHT attribution.

rulings.title: operation of Australia's permanent establishment attribution rules

nodes.label: Apply the DTA Article 5 PE definition
nodes.body: Art 5(1): a fixed place of business through which the business is wholly or partly carried on. Art 5(2): specific inclusions (place of management, branch, office, factory, workshop, extraction, agricultural property, building site >9 months, dredging ≥6 months). Each DTA varies — check the specific treaty.

nodes.label: Is there a fixed place of business through which business is carried on (Art 5(1))?
nodes.body: Requires a distinct geographic location with some degree of permanence. Rented or controlled space suffices; temporary or purely preparatory locations may not.

nodes.label: No fixed place — check Art 5(4) deeming limbs (dependent agent, substantial equipment, supervisory)?
nodes.body: Without a fixed place under Art 5(1), there is no PE unless one of the Art 5(4) deeming limbs applies: (a) dependent agent with contract authority, (b) substantial equipment rental >12 months, (c) supervisory >9 months, (d) substantial processing. Art 5(5) independent agent exception then applies.

nodes.label: Does an Art 5(2) inclusion apply (building site >9 months, dredging ≥6 months)?
nodes.body: e.g. US DTA: building site/construction/assembly/installation project >9 months (Art 5(2)(h)); installation/drilling rig or ship for dredging or seabed exploration ≥6 months in any 24-month period (Art 5(2)(i)). Other DTAs differ (some 12 months) — always check the specific treaty.

nodes.label: Do the Art 5(3) preparatory/auxiliary exclusions apply?
nodes.body: Art 5(3): storage/display/delivery facilities, stock maintenance for storage/display/delivery/processing, purchasing or information collection, preparatory/auxiliary activities (advertising, research), short building sites, short dredging use.

nodes.label: Is there a dependent agent with authority to conclude contracts (Art 5(4))?
nodes.body: Art 5(4)(a): deemed PE where a person (other than independent agent) has and habitually exercises authority to conclude contracts. Art 5(4)(b)-(d): substantial equipment rental >12 months, supervisory >9 months, substantial processing. Also check Art 5(6) subsidiary carve-out separately.

nodes.label: Is the agent of independent status (Art 5(5))?
nodes.body: Art 5(5): broker, general commission agent or independent agent acting in the ordinary course is not a PE. Factual test — independence, arm's length, ordinary-course activity.

nodes.label: Treaty PE exists
nodes.body: Australia may tax profits attributable to the PE (Art 7). Attribution per TR 2001/11 and Div 815 transfer pricing.

satisfying the carrying on a business at or through a permanent establishment

nodes.label: Confirm: No treaty PE
nodes.body: Art 7 does not apply, but other articles (royalties, dividends, independent personal services) may still tax specific income.

nodes.label: Facet — Treaty priority: which definition applies?
nodes.body: Where to look: International Tax Agreements Act 1953 s 4(2) (treaties prevail over the ITAA 1936/1997 where inconsistent); s 23AH(15) (PE in s 23AH follows the DTA where one affects the person); s 44(7) (PE meaning for s 44 follows the DTA, else s 6(1)). The domestic definition still applies for non-treaty purposes — e.g. non-treaty residents, and provisions that do not adopt the DTA meaning.

nodes.label: Facet — Agency PE limbs: domestic (a)/(e)/(f) vs treaty Art 5(4)/(5)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 6(1)(a),(e),(f) (domestic — agent place, bona fide commission agent exclusion, no-general-authority exclusion); Art 5(4)-(5) (treaty — dependent agent with contract authority, independent agent exception). Note the differences: the domestic definition's para (f) exclusion turns on the agent's authority to negotiate and conclude contracts; the treaty's Art 5(4) turns on authority to conclude contracts habitually exercised. TR 2002/5 analyses both.

rulings.title: What is a place at or through which a person carries on any business

nodes.label: Facet — Attributable profits once a PE is confirmed
nodes.body: Where to look: TR 2001/11 (attribution rules), TR 2014/3 (carrying on business at/through PE), Div 815 ITAA 1997 (transfer pricing). The OECD authorised OECD approach (AOA) and the 'functionally separate entity' principle govern how much profit is attributable to the PE. s 128B ITAA 1936 attributes interest/royalty income to a PE.

nodes.label: Facet — Treaty variations: does the DTA use different thresholds?
nodes.body: Where to look: the specific DTA. US DTA Art 5(2)(h): building site >9 months. Many older DTAs (e.g. UK, Japan, Singapore) use 12 months; some use 6 months. Dredging/exploration thresholds vary (6 months in US; others differ). Always verify the specific treaty's Art 5 — the explorer's treaties collection holds the full text per country.

nodes.label: No domestic PE
nodes.body: The domestic s 6(1) definition does not treat any place as a permanent establishment of the person. Note: this does not preclude treaty-based PE conclusions under a DTA.

nodes.label: Is the PE asserted only because of control by / being controlled by a resident company?
nodes.body: Art 5(6): The fact that a company which is a resident of a Contracting State controls or is controlled by a company which is a resident of the other Contracting State, or which carries on business in that other State (whether through a permanent establishment or otherwise), shall not of itself constitute either company a permanent establishment of the other.
